items.notes: Off cuts both inputs. With a USB wall charger and a solar panel both connected, Force USB and Force Solar switch the board between them in either direction, Force Solar holds with USB present, and Auto leaves a working input alone or, from a cold start, enables USB (port 1). If the charger overrides a forced choice, the drop-down falls back to Auto and the log says so.
Read USB, Solar or None, matching the measured `VBUS` (about 5 V and about 13 V). The "USB or Solar" reading, shown when both could be feeding the board, was not seen.
The charger clears its MPPT enable bit when it rejects an input. The driver turns it on again at the next poll and logs it.
With low and critical charge selected, `FG_ALERT` went low while the gauge reported them, on two boards. The gauge ships with the register at 0 and never asserts the pin until it is written.
On the first boot with a 4000 mAh LiFePO4 cell it wrote the design capacity and energy, the alert configuration and the sense-resistor calibration. Each value read back correctly.

items.feature: Offset calibration buttons and Enable Impedance Track
items.notes: Planned on a lithium-ion board: calibrate with the charger off and the pack at rest, then enable Impedance Track and run a charge and discharge cycle.
The driver should log an error at boot if the gauge is running a different chemistry.
Pulling `FG_ALERT` low by hand woke the board, reported as an ext1 wake on GPIO4. A real alert from the gauge while asleep has not been tried.

items.feature: Prevent Deep Sleep survives a reboot
items.notes: The switch reads a flag kept in flash, so it should hold through resets and power cycles.
At the cutoff voltage the CPU loop, the status LED and the user rail went off.
Added because the radio kept drawing about 135 mA after the cutoff.
The gauge pulled `FG_ALERT` low and the pin woke the board. The wake was tested with the pin grounded by hand.
Encrypted updates work. A blank board running the stock ESPHome web image refuses an encrypted update, so the first flash has to go over USB.
Compiles for the ESP32-C5 and runs on the bench boards.
The configuration validates. It has not been flashed to a board and run through setup.
